title: Mljet Travel Guide: National Park, Ferries & Where to Stay
metaDescription: Plan a trip to Mljet, Croatia. Factual guide covering National Park access, driving routes, ferries, best villages to stay in, and practical tips.
intro:
Mljet is a heavily forested Adriatic island suited for travelers seeking nature, hiking, and quiet coastal villages. The western third of the island is a protected National Park featuring two saltwater lakes, drawing day-trippers and extended stay visitors alike. The eastern and central parts offer isolated bays and sandy beaches, distinct from the typical Croatian pebble coastline.

The main travel season runs from late May to September. July and August bring the warmest sea temperatures and the highest volume of yacht traffic, particularly in Pomena and Polače. May and September offer milder weather for cycling and walking the National Park trails, with fewer crowds and lower accommodation rates.

areas.name: Pomena
areas.parking: Limited street parking; paid lot near the hotel
areas.summary: A small port village at the western tip, serving as the main entrance to the National Park. It has the island's only large hotel, high yacht traffic, and numerous seafood restaurants.

areas.name: Polače
areas.parking: Street parking available, congested in peak season
areas.beach: Rocky waterfront; 3 km walk/cycle to the lakes
areas.summary: Features prominent Roman ruins right on the waterfront. It acts as the secondary entrance to the National Park and sits in a deep, protected bay with several ferry connections.

areas.name: Saplunara
areas.parking: Private spots at apartments, small unpaved lots
areas.beach: Direct access to rare sandy beaches
areas.summary: Located on the isolated eastern tip of the island, known for its sandy bays. There are no National Park attractions here, making it quieter and entirely focused on beachgoing.

areas.name: Sobra
areas.parking: Ample parking near the ferry port and village center
areas.beach: Small pebble and rocky spots in the village
areas.summary: The main port where the car ferry from the mainland arrives. It is centrally located, offering lower prices and a strategic base for driving to both ends of the island.

whenToGo: The tourist season on Mljet runs from May to October, aligning with expanded ferry schedules and open restaurants. July and August are the busiest and most expensive months, with sea temperatures reaching 27°C and large numbers of yachts docking in Pomena and Polače. May, June, and September offer pleasant air temperatures around 20–25°C, making these months ideal for cycling and hiking in the National Park, though the sea may be too cool for extended swimming in early May. Between November and April, the island is very quiet; passenger catamarans operate on reduced schedules, and most tourist facilities, including many restaurants and accommodations, close for the winter.

faq.question: Is Mljet worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, for travelers seeking nature, hiking, and clear water away from large resort towns. The island's National Park and saltwater lakes offer a distinct landscape compared to other Croatian islands, though it lacks nightlife and extensive shopping.

faq.question: How many days do I need in Mljet?
faq.answer: Two to three days are sufficient to cycle around the National Park lakes, visit St. Mary's Island, and explore a few coastal villages. Day trips from Dubrovnik or Korčula are popular, but staying overnight allows you to experience the park without the midday crowds.

faq.question: Which is the best beach on Mljet?
faq.answer: Velika Saplunara and Mala Saplunara on the eastern tip are the best sandy beaches. In the National Park, the shores of Malo Jezero and Veliko Jezero (the saltwater lakes) are highly popular for swimming due to their warm, calm waters and pine shade.

faq.question: Do I need a car on Mljet?
faq.answer: A car or scooter is highly recommended if you plan to explore the island, as the distance between the National Park in the west and Saplunara in the east is over 40 kilometers. If you only intend to stay in Pomena or Polače and visit the National Park, a car is unnecessary.

faq.question: Where do I park in Mljet National Park?
faq.answer: There is a designated paid parking lot in the village of Vrbovica (near Mali Most) right at the lake entrance, as well as street parking in Pomena and Polače. Vehicles are not allowed on the walking paths directly surrounding the saltwater lakes.

faq.question: Is Mljet good for families?
faq.answer: Yes, especially for active families who enjoy cycling, swimming, and nature walks. The saltwater lakes are very safe for children due to the lack of waves, and the sandy beaches in Saplunara feature shallow, gradual entries.
